The lab lists db.client.operation.duration in Splunk Observability Cloud before and after, and reads Postgres query p95 in milliseconds through the SignalFlow stream.

files.content:
# Read Postgres Query p95 in Splunk With One OTel Java Agent Setting

## What it shows

A small Spring Boot system runs on EKS: `orders` calls `inventory`, and `inventory` reads Postgres. Both run the OpenTelemetry Java agent 2.33.1 and send to the Splunk OTel Collector. Each run prints the agent's version line.

* `reproduce.sh` (BEFORE): installs the Collector, builds the jar once in the cluster, attaches the agent with its default settings, runs a fixed load, and lists the database metrics Splunk Observability Cloud holds for the environment.
* `fix.sh` (BUILD): adds one environment variable to each service, `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database`, runs the same load rate, and reads the new `db.client.operation.duration` metric back from Splunk: its time series through `/v2/metrictimeseries`, and its p95 in milliseconds through the SignalFlow stream.

The setting is the only change. The jar's SHA-256, the image and `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` are printed and compared across the two runs. The Collector chart keeps its default values.

## What the setting does

The agent records `db.client.operation.duration`, a histogram in seconds, once a service opts in to the stable database conventions. Set it as an environment variable or as the system property `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in=database`, because the agent reads it at startup from those two places. `check.sh` runs the same value from the agent's configuration file too and prints what that run exports.

The stable conventions also bring new names for database span attributes and connection pool metrics. `check.sh` prints both sets. `database/dup` emits the old and new names together, which suits a team moving dashboards across, and `check.sh` runs that as well.

## How the p95 is read

With the Collector chart's default values, this histogram reaches Splunk as `db.client.operation.duration_bucket` with an `le` dimension, plus `_count`, `_sum`, `_min` and `_max`. The scripts print the exporter's histogram setting and the raw metric names, and `lib.sh` holds the Splunk reads. This SignalFlow program gives the p95 in milliseconds:

```python
data('db.client.operation.duration_bucket', filter=filter('deployment.environment', 'YOUR_ENV'), rollup='delta').sum(by=['le']).histogram_percentile(pct=95, bucket_name='le').scale(1000).publish('p95_ms')
```

The agent exports once a minute, so `fix.sh` takes one reading per full minute of steady load and reports the median. It computes the same p95 from the bucket counts, prints the difference between the two, and compares the queries Splunk counted with the requests the load sent. `fixed` needs that comparison to land within 10%.

A percentile from a histogram is an estimate inside one bucket, so the script prints the bucket that holds the p95 along with the boundaries Splunk stores. It also prints the series for each distinct query and service, which is what a team multiplies by when it rolls this out, and the CPU steal on the node during the load.

Each order reads one of the 100 seeded rows, because `inventory` maps every order ID with `id % 100 + 1`. A run with any load errors stops before a reading counts.

## Timing

The BEFORE load runs for 120 seconds to fit the 14-minute limit on a script, because it only has to show which metrics arrive. The BUILD load runs for 300 seconds so at least three full minutes can be read. Both send one request every 50 ms.

## Run it

Set `AWS_REGION`, `LAB_NAME`, `TF_VAR_lab_name` (the same value as `LAB_NAME`), `SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (ingest) and `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` (read). Then run:

```bash
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
./reproduce.sh
./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

The run uses two `t3.large` nodes and an EKS control plane for about an hour. Each latency figure comes from one cluster and one load rate on burstable instances, so read your own service's numbers before you set a target.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, run on a GitHub runner with Docker before AWS is paid for. It uses the lab's own source, images,
# agent and load script, and proves one setting makes the agent emit db.client.operation.duration. Kubernetes and Splunk
# are tested by the rehearsal. No secrets are used here.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/src c/out c/init c/load

METRIC=db.client.operation.duration

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
open("c/src/pom.xml", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "pom.xml"))
open("c/src/App.java", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "App.java"))
open("c/init/init.sql", "w").write(block("k8s/10-app.yaml", "init.sql"))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY

IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'maven:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
PY_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ ]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
PG_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'postgres:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
AGENT_URL=$(grep -m1 -oE 'https://github.com/[^"]+\.jar' k8s/00-build.yaml)
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== Fetching the agent and building the jar"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$PY_IMAGE" python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlretrieve('$AGENT_URL', '/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar')"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  set -e; mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab; cp /src/pom.xml /w/; cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/; cd /w
  mvn -q -B -DskipTests package; cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar'
ls -l c/out

docker run -d --name postgres --network lab -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=lab -v "$PWD/c/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro" "$PG_IMAGE" >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
sleep 3

start() {   # name, then any extra docker arguments. The agent options are the same in both runs.
  local name=$1; shift
  docker run -d --name "$name" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab:ro" --entrypoint java "$@" \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=postgres \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=lab -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8080 \
    -e "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$name -Dotel.traces.exporter=console -Dotel.metrics.exporter=console -Dotel.metric.export.interval=5000 -Dotel.logs.exporter=none" \
    "$IMAGE" -Xms256m -Xmx256m -jar /lab/app.jar >/dev/null
}
ready() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'process running for [0-9.]+' | tail -1 | sed "s/^/$1 /"
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' || { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1; }
}
load() { docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e SECONDS_TOTAL=20 -e SECONDS_WARM=5 "$PY_IMAGE" python /load/load.py; }
db_names() { grep -oE 'name=db\.[a-z._]+' "$1" | sort -u | sed 's/name=//' || true; }

span_keys() { grep LoggingSpanExporter "$1" | grep -E ' CLIENT .*db\.' | tail -1 | grep -oE '\bdb\.[a-z_.]+=' | tr -d = | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; echo; }
exports() { grep -c "name=$METRIC," "$1" || true; }

run() {   # name, then any extra docker arguments for both services
  local name=$1; shift
  docker rm -f orders inventory >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  start inventory "$@"
  start orders "$@"
  ready inventory
  ready orders
  load | tee "c/$name.txt"
  grep -q 'errors=0' "c/$name.txt" || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: requests failed in the $name run"; exit 1; }
  sleep 8
  { docker logs orders 2>&1; docker logs inventory 2>&1; } > "c/$name.log"
  echo "-- $name run: database metric names"
  db_names "c/$name.log" | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "-- $name run: database span attribute keys: $(span_keys "c/$name.log")"
  echo "$METRIC exports in the $name run: $(exports "c/$name.log")"
}

echo "== The agent with its default settings"
run default
grep -m1 -h 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' c/default.log || true
echo "== The same agent options, with OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database"
run setting -e OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database
echo "== The same agent options, with OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database/dup, which emits both sets of names"
run dup -e OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database/dup
echo "== The same agent options, with the setting in the agent's configuration file"
echo 'otel.semconv-stability.opt-in=database' > c/out/otel.properties
run file -e OTEL_JAVAAGENT_CONFIGURATION_FILE=/lab/otel.properties
BEFORE=$(exports c/default.log)
AFTER=$(exports c/setting.log)
DUP=$(exports c/dup.log)

# The last export holds the running totals: what the agent would send to the Collector, in seconds.
python3 - <<'PY' | tee c/point.txt
import re
lines = [l for l in open("c/setting.log") if "name=db.client.operation.duration," in l]
if not lines:
    raise SystemExit(0)
text = lines[-1]
print("unit", re.search(r"unit=(\w+)", text)[1], "type", re.search(r"unit=\w+, type=(\w+)", text)[1])
points = re.findall(r"getAttributes=\w*\{([^}]*)\}, getSum=[^,]+, getCount=(\d+).*?getBoundaries=\[([^\]]*)\], getCounts=\[([^\]]*)\]", text)
for attributes, count, boundaries, counts in points:
    print("attributes", attributes)
    print("point queries", count, "boundaries", boundaries, "counts", counts)
print("queries", sum(int(p[1]) for p in points))
PY

[ "$BEFORE" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the default settings already export $METRIC"; exit 1; }
[ "$AFTER" -ge 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the setting did not export $METRIC"; exit 1; }
[ "$DUP" -ge 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: database/dup did not export $METRIC"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'db.system.name=postgresql' c/point.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the metric has no Postgres attribute"; exit 1; }
QUERIES=$(awk '$1 == "queries" {print $2}' c/point.txt)
SENT=$(grep -oE 'requests=[0-9]+' c/setting.txt | cut -d= -f2)
echo "queries in the metric: $QUERIES, requests measured after warm-up: $SENT"
[ "${QUERIES:-0}" -ge "${SENT:-1}" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the metric counted fewer queries than requests"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: one environment variable on each service. Same jar, image, agent options and Collector, and no code change.
# Then read the new metric back from Splunk: its series, and its query p95 in milliseconds through SignalFlow.
# Splunk reads and arithmetic live in lib.sh.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=830
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_fixed"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_API_TOKEN is not set"
source ./lib.sh
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"
newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }

echo "== 2. The whole change: one environment variable on each service"
for s in orders inventory; do
  kubectl -n demo set env "deployment/$s" OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=database >/dev/null || fail "could not set the variable on $s"
done
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 400)s" >/dev/null || fail "inventory did not roll out"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 400)s" >/dev/null || fail "orders did not roll out"

: > agent-options-after.txt
for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s effective setting: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- printenv OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN)"
  kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name == "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS") | .value' >> agent-options-after.txt
  kubectl -n demo logs "$p" -c app 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' | sed "s/^/$s /"
done
same=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$same" = "$(cat jar-sha.txt)" ] && echo "jar unchanged from the before run" || fail "the jar changed, so the comparison would be unfair"
cmp -s agent-options.txt agent-options-after.txt && echo "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS unchanged from the before run" || fail "the agent options changed, so the comparison would be unfair"
exporter_config

echo "== 3. The load: one request every 50 ms for 300 seconds, the first 30 seconds as warm-up"
read -r steal0 total0 <<<"$(cpu_stat "$(newest inventory)")"
t_load=$(date +%s)
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 330 200)s" || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; fail "the load did not finish"; }
t_end=$(date +%s)
kubectl -n demo logs load | tee load-after.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' load-after.txt || fail "the load saw errors, so this run can't be used"
read -r steal1 total1 <<<"$(cpu_stat "$(newest inventory)")"
echo "CPU steal on the app node during the load: $(awk -v s=$(( ${steal1:-0} - ${steal0:-0} )) -v t=$(( ${total1:-0} - ${total0:-0} )) 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", (t > 0 ? s / t * 100 : 0)}')%"

# One reading per minute. The agent exports every 60 seconds, so a reading covers the minute before it, and the first
# starts after the warm-up. A full minute holds the load's own rate, so a partial last minute is dropped by count.
sent=$(grep -oE 'requests=[0-9]+' load-after.txt | cut -d= -f2)
per_minute=$(awk -v r="${sent:-0}" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", r / 270 * 60}')
least=$(awk -v m="$per_minute" 'BEGIN{printf "%d", m * 0.9}')
from_ms=$(( (t_load + 90) * 1000 ))
to_ms=$(( t_end * 1000 ))
F="filter('deployment.environment', '${LAB_NAME}')"
BUCKETS="data('${METRIC}_bucket', filter=${F}, rollup='delta').sum(by=['le']).publish('buckets')"
COUNT="data('${METRIC}_count', filter=${F}, rollup='delta').sum().publish('queries')"
P95="data('${METRIC}_bucket', filter=${F}, rollup='delta').sum(by=['le']).histogram_percentile(pct=95, bucket_name='le').scale(1000).publish('p95_ms')"

echo "== 4. Reading the metric back from Splunk Observability Cloud"
count=0; n=0; pts=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 320 30)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  count=$(duration_series | jq -r '.results | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    signalflow "$BUCKETS" "$from_ms" "$to_ms" > points-buckets.jsonl
    signalflow "$COUNT" "$from_ms" "$to_ms" > points-count.jsonl
    pts=$(minutes points-buckets.jsonl points-count.jsonl "$least")
    n=$(grep -c . <<<"$pts" || true)
  fi
  echo "  t+$(( $(date +%s) - t_end ))s after the load: series=${count:-0} full one-minute readings=${n:-0}"
  [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${n:-0}" -ge 3 ] && break
  sleep 20
done
[ "${n:-0}" -ge 1 ] || { echo "SignalFlow reply: $(head -c 400 signalflow.txt | tr '\n' ' ')"; fail "no readings came back from the SignalFlow stream"; }

echo "-- $METRIC in Splunk, from /v2/metrictimeseries"
breakdown
echo "time series for $METRIC with the setting: ${count:-0}"
echo "-- database metric names in Splunk with the setting"
raw_names "sf_metric:db.* AND deployment.environment:${LAB_NAME}" | sed 's/^/  /'

echo "-- one-minute readings from the bucket and count series"
jq -r '"  minute ending \(.ts / 1000 | todate): queries=\(.queries) p95_ms=\(.p95_ms * 100 | round / 100) in the bucket \(.lower_ms) to \(.upper_ms) ms"' <<<"$pts"
echo "-- the same p95 from SignalFlow's histogram_percentile()"
echo "  program: $P95"
full=$(jq -sc 'map(.ts)' <<<"$pts")
native=$(signalflow "$P95" "$from_ms" "$to_ms" | jq -r --argjson full "$full" 'select(.ts as $t | $full | index($t)) | .value' 2>/dev/null)
grep . <<<"$native" | sed 's/^/  p95_ms reading: /'
[ -n "$native" ] || echo "  SignalFlow reply: $(head -c 300 signalflow.txt | tr '\n' ' ')"

by_buckets=$(jq -r '.p95_ms' <<<"$pts" | median)
got=$(grep -c . <<<"$native" || true)
# One result per reading is a single p95 series, so anything else stays as printed evidence only.
if [ "${got:-0}" -ge 1 ] && [ "${got:-0}" -le "$n" ]; then p95=$(grep . <<<"$native" | median); src="histogram_percentile()"; else p95=$by_buckets; src="the bucket series"; fi
p95=$(awk -v v="$p95" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", v}')
diff=$(awk -v a="$p95" -v b="$by_buckets" 'BEGIN{d = a - b; printf "%.2f", (d < 0 ? -d : d)}')
lower=$(jq -r '.lower_ms' <<<"$pts" | median)
upper=$(jq -r '.upper_ms' <<<"$pts" | median)
queries=$(jq -rs 'map(.queries) | add' <<<"$pts")
expected=$(awk -v m="$per_minute" -v n="$n" 'BEGIN{printf "%d", m * n}')
gap=$(awk -v q="$queries" -v e="$expected" 'BEGIN{d = (q - e) / e * 100; printf "%.1f", (d < 0 ? -d : d)}')
echo "median query p95 from Splunk: $p95 ms from $src, over $n one-minute readings"
echo "the two methods differ by $diff ms, and the bucket series gives $(awk -v v="$by_buckets" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", v}') ms"
echo "the p95 falls in the bucket from $lower to $upper ms"
echo "queries Splunk counted: $queries, requests the load sent in the same minutes: $expected, a gap of ${gap}%"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: db_duration_series_after=${count:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: query_p95_ms=$p95"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: query_p95_minutes=$n"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: query_p95_bucket_upper_ms=$upper"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: queries_gap_pct=$gap"

if [ "${count:-0}" -ge 1 ] && [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && awk -v v="$p95" -v g="$gap" 'BEGIN{exit !(v > 0 && g <= 10)}'; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-src
  namespace: demo
data:
  pom.xml: |
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
             xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
             xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
      <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
      <parent>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId>
        <version>3.5.6</version>
        <relativePath/>
      </parent>
      <groupId>lab</groupId>
      <artifactId>app</artifactId>
      <version>1.0.0</version>
      <properties>
        <java.version>21</java.version>
      </properties>
      <dependencies>
        <dependency>
          <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
          <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
          <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
          <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-jdbc</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
          <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
          <artifactId>postgresql</artifactId>
          <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>
      </dependencies>
      <build>
        <finalName>app</finalName>
        <plugins>
          <plugin>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          </plugin>
        </plugins>
      </build>
    </project>
  App.java: |
    package lab;

    import java.util.Map;
    import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
    import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
    import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
    import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;
    import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
    import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
    import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
    import org.springframework.web.client.RestClient;

    @SpringBootApplication
    @RestController
    public class App {
      private final JdbcTemplate jdbc;
      private final RestClient inventory;

      public App(JdbcTemplate jdbc, RestClient.Builder builder, @Value("${inventory.url}") String url) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.inventory = builder.baseUrl(url).build();
      }

      public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(App.class, args);
      }

      @GetMapping("/orders/{id}")
      public Map<String, Object> order(@PathVariable("id") long id) {
        Map<?, ?> stock = inventory.get().uri("/stock/{id}", id).retrieve().body(Map.class);
        return Map.of("order", id, "stock", stock);
      }

      @GetMapping("/stock/{id}")
      public Map<String, Object> stock(@PathVariable("id") long id) {
        return jdbc.queryForMap("select sku, qty from stock where id = ?", id % 100 + 1);
      }
    }
---
# Builds the jar once and fetches the agent once. Both land on the app node, so every run uses the same files.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: build
  namespace: demo
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 420
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: src
          configMap:
            name: app-src
        - name: lab
          hostPath:
            path: /opt/lab
            type: DirectoryOrCreate
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-agent
          image: python:3.12-slim
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab }
          command:
            - python
            - -c
            - |
              import time, urllib.request
              url = "https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/releases/download/v2.33.1/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar"
              for attempt in range(1, 13):
                  try:
                      urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, "/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar")
                      print("agent downloaded on attempt", attempt)
                      break
                  except Exception as e:
                      print("download attempt", attempt, "failed:", e)
                      time.sleep(10)
              else:
                  raise SystemExit("the agent could not be downloaded")
      containers:
        - name: build
          image: maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-21
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: src, mountPath: /src }
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab }
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              set -e
              mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab
              cp /src/pom.xml /w/pom.xml
              cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/App.java
              cd /w
              mvn -q -B -DskipTests package
              cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar
              ls -l /lab

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Sends one order request every 50 ms, and each order reads Postgres once through inventory, at the same rate in every run.
    # inventory maps every order ID onto one of the 100 seeded rows with id % 100 + 1, so each lookup finds a row.
    import http.client, os, random, sys, time
    seconds, warm = int(os.environ["SECONDS_TOTAL"]), int(os.environ["SECONDS_WARM"])
    conn, took, errors, last, gap = http.client.HTTPConnection("orders", 8080, timeout=10), [], 0, "", 0.05
    start = time.time()
    while time.time() - start < seconds:
        sent = time.time()
        last = "%032x" % random.getrandbits(128)
        try:
            conn.request("GET", "/orders/%d" % random.randint(1, 1000), headers={"traceparent": "00-%s-%016x-01" % (last, random.getrandbits(64))})
            r = conn.getresponse(); r.read()
            ok = r.status == 200
        except Exception:
            ok = False
            conn.close()
        ms = (time.time() - sent) * 1000
        if not ok:
            errors += 1
        elif sent - start >= warm:
            took.append(ms)
        time.sleep(max(0, gap - ms / 1000))
    took.sort()
    if not took:
        print("LOAD no successful requests after warm-up, errors=%d" % errors)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("LOAD requests=%d errors=%d p50_ms=%.2f p95_ms=%.2f" % (len(took), errors, took[len(took) // 2], took[int(len(took) * 0.95)]))
    print("LOAD last_trace_id=%s" % last)
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: SECONDS_TOTAL, value: "300" }
        - { name: SECONDS_WARM, value: "30" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: a Spring Boot orders service calls an inventory service, which reads Postgres. The Collector runs, and the
# OTel Java agent is attached with its default settings. This records which database metrics Splunk holds at the start.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=810
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_reproduced"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o wide || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# The app stays on one node and the load generator on the other, in both runs.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_API_TOKEN is not set"
source ./lib.sh
echo "lab name, new for every run, so Splunk holds nothing older under this environment: $LAB_NAME"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1) first, the same in both measurements"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"
exporter_config

echo "== 3. Building the jar in the cluster, once, and fetching the agent"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 430 300)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --all-containers --tail=20 2>/dev/null || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying Postgres, orders and inventory"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the app"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/postgres --timeout="$(cap 90 200)s" || fail "postgres did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 180)s" || fail "inventory did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" || fail "orders did not start"

echo "== 5. Attaching the agent with its default settings: one environment variable on each service"
for s in orders inventory; do
  kubectl -n demo set env "deployment/$s" "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$s -Dotel.exporter.otlp.endpoint=http://\$(HOST_IP):4318 -Dotel.resource.attributes=deployment.environment=$LAB_NAME,deployment.environment.name=$LAB_NAME -Dotel.logs.exporter=none" >/dev/null || fail "could not attach the agent to $s"
done
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" >/dev/null || fail "inventory did not roll out"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" >/dev/null || fail "orders did not roll out"

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }

: > agent-options.txt
for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
  echo "$s semconv opt-in settings: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(. == "OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN")] | length')"
  kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name == "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS") | .value' >> agent-options.txt
  kubectl -n demo logs "$p" -c app 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' | sed "s/^/$s /"
done
kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}' > jar-sha.txt

echo "== 6. A fixed load: one request every 50 ms for 120 seconds, which is enough to show what arrives"
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e 's/value: "300"/value: "120"/' k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 150 15)s" || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; fail "the load did not finish"; }
kubectl -n demo logs load | tee load-before.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' load-before.txt || fail "the load saw errors, so this run can't be used"

echo "== 7. What Splunk Observability Cloud holds for this environment"
http=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 270 20)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  http=$(series "sf_metric:http.server.request.duration* AND deployment.environment:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.results | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  echo "  t+$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s after the load: HTTP server metric series=${http:-0}"
  [ "${http:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 20
done
[ "${http:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "the agent's HTTP metric has not reached Splunk yet, so this before-state can't be read"
echo "-- database metrics in Splunk with the default settings"
raw_names "sf_metric:db.* AND deployment.environment:${LAB_NAME}" | sed 's/^/  /'
before=$(duration_series | jq -r '.results | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
echo "time series for $METRIC with the default settings: ${before:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: db_duration_series_before=${before:-0}"

[ "${before:-0}" -eq 0 ] && emit reproduced || emit not_reproduced
